Annual site energy consumption before and after envelope upgrades Figure 2 further breaks down the annual energy savings for the dwelling unit, showing the impact of each individual measure and the combined effect of the full envelope upgrade package. Advanced air sealing provides the largest savings at 30.2 MBtu, followed by duct sealing and insulation (12.8 MBtu). Attic floor insulation alone contributes a modest 2.4 MBtu. When all measures are implemented together, total savings reach 42.5 MBtu, which is slightly lower than the sum of the individual impacts. However, with only one example dwelling unit, it is difficult to determine whether combined measures consistently result in higher or lower savings than the sum of individual impacts. A broader assessment will be conducted in the stock-level analysis in Section 4.2. Figure 2. Therefore, this section analyzes 15-minute time- series data for these end uses under the full envelope package upgrade and each individual measures applied separately. Heating end uses include heating and heating fans/pumps. Cooling end uses include cooling and cooling fans/pumps. January 2 is selected to examine the heating time-series data, while July 2 is selected to examine the cooling time-series data. Figure 3 shows that each envelope upgrade reduces heating energy consumption compared to the baseline. The combined upgrade package (dark blue line) consistently shows the lowest heating energy consumption throughout the day, indicating cumulative savings from all measures. The sudden drop in heating energy consumption at 2:15 and the rise at 11:15 are caused by changes in the heating setpoint temperature. At 2:00, the setpoint drops from 70°F to 67°F, eliminating the need for heating and resulting in zero energy use from 2:00 to 2:15. At 11:00, the setpoint increases from 67°F to 70°F, triggering a spike in heating energy use from 11:00 to 11:15.
